newsitem.title: UK: New resignation hits embattled Conservative Party.
newsitem.headline: New resignation hits embattled Conservative Party.

text.p: Britain's embattled Conservative Party, beset by allegations of sleaze in the runup to a general election, was hit by further controversy on Saturday when the party's Scottish chief stepped down because of his private life.
Sir Michael Hirst, chairman of the Conservative Party in Scotland, said in a letter to Prime Minister John Major that he was resigning rather than embarrass the party.

"I very deeply regret these circumstances which have caused great distress to my family and which may, I fear, cause embarrassment to the party in the current climate," he said in a letter broadcast on British radio.
The letter gave no details about the reasons for his resignation but referred only to a past indiscretion in his private life.
Opinion polls say the opposition Labour Party led by Tony Blair will sweep to power in the May 1 election and unseat prime Minister John major.
Labour stepped up pressure on Saturday on Conservative MPs embroiled in sleaze allegations as the campaign fell hostage to sex and money scandals.

With Conservative MP Piers Merchant in hiding after reports of an extramarital affair with a 17-year-old nightclub hostess, attention turned back to former junior minister Neil Hamilton, who is accused of taking thousands of pounds in cash to ask questions in parliament.
Hamilton again denied the allegations, which surfaced more than two years ago, in a letter to The Times newspaper saying he had a right to a fair hearing.

But the Labour candidate set to stand against Hamilton in the staunchly Conservative seat of Tatton, central England, said on Saturday he was prepared to step down to make way for a non-political "anti-corruption" candidate.
Labour's Jon Kelly said he hoped the move would shame Hamilton into quitting.
"Neil Hamilton is a symbol of all that is wrong with John Major's government -- weak leadership, dither, double standards and sleaze," Kelly's campaign manager Ian McCartney told a news conference.
The minority Liberal Democrat Party said it was seriously considering joining Labour's initiative and withdrawing its own candidate in Tatton.
The Conservative Party, some 25 points behind Labour in national opinion polls, dismissed the move as an election stunt in a seat which Labour had no hope of winning in the election.
Sleaze has dominated the headlines ever since Major set the election date two weeks ago and has thwarted Conservative attempts to capitalise on good economic news.

Another Conservative MP, who admitted taking cash from Harrods Egytpian-born boss Mohammed Al Fayed to ask questions on his behalf in parliament, resigned earlier this week and a third Conservative MP stepped down after reports linking him to a married woman he is said to have met while attending a clinic for alcoholics.

Piers Merchant, the MP who has been pictured in a tabloid newspaper apparently fondling a mini-skirted blonde teenager, left his home via the backdoor on Friday to escape from journalists besieging his family's home.
He has vehemently denied having an affair with the 17-year-old but has been told by senior Conservatives to clear up the allegations swiftly.
